definition_zh: 异常；反常；畸形；异常事物
definition_en: the state of being abnormal, or a feature, condition or event that departs from the normal
core_image: 一排整齐的砖里夹着一块歪斜的，一眼就看出不对
scene: 产检的屏幕上，医生停在一处反复放大查看。 The scan revealed a small abnormality in the baby's heart.
sceneCN: 这里 abnormality 是「异常结构、畸形」（第 2 个义项：身体结构上的异常）；句意为扫描发现婴儿心脏有一处小的异常。

derivatives.zh: abnormality 的形容词对应形式，义为「反常的；异常的」
由 abnormal 加 -ly 构成副词，义为「异常地」
与本词同根的肯定形式，义为「正常的；标准的」

senses.title: The state of being abnormal
senses.definition: the condition of differing from what is usual or expected
senses.definitionCN: 与通常或预期情况不同的状态
senses.example: The report noted the abnormality of the reading without explaining it.
senses.exampleCN: 报告指出了读数的异常，却没有解释原因。
senses.why: The noun names the state itself, the quality that the adjective abnormal describes.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词指状态本身，也就是形容词 abnormal 所描述的那种性质。

senses.title: A physical malformation
senses.definition: a structural defect or unusual formation in a body part or organ
senses.definitionCN: 身体部位或器官上的结构缺陷或不寻常形态
senses.example: The ultrasound found an abnormality in the kidney.
senses.exampleCN: 超声检查发现肾脏有一处畸形。
senses.why: Medicine turns the abstract state into a countable thing: one specific place where the body departs from its form.
senses.whyCN: 医学把抽象状态变成可数的事物：身体偏离应有形态的某一个具体位置。

senses.title: An anomalous test value
senses.definition: a measurement or finding that falls outside the healthy reference range
senses.definitionCN: 落在健康参考范围之外的测量值或发现
senses.example: The lab flagged two abnormalities in the blood sample.
senses.exampleCN: 实验室标出了血样中的两处异常。
senses.why: A reading away from the healthy line is packaged as a countable abnormality for the report.
senses.whyCN: 偏离健康线的读数被打包成报告里可数的「异常项」。

senses.title: Irregularity in behaviour
senses.definition: a pattern of behaviour that departs from what is expected or accepted
senses.definitionCN: 偏离预期或被接受标准的行为模式
senses.example: Teachers were trained to notice behavioural abnormalities early.
senses.exampleCN: 教师们受过训练，要及早注意行为上的反常。
senses.why: Behaviour can also be measured against a social line, and a deviation becomes a named abnormality.
senses.whyCN: 行为同样可以对着社会那条线来衡量，偏离就被命名为异常。

senses.title: A statistical deviation
senses.definition: a data point or pattern that lies far from the expected distribution
senses.definitionCN: 远离预期分布的数据点或模式
senses.example: The system reported an abnormality in the overnight figures.
senses.exampleCN: 系统报告了夜间数据中的一处异常。
senses.why: Once a baseline is drawn, anything far from it can be listed as an abnormality in the data.
senses.whyCN: 基线一旦画出，离它很远的东西就能被列为数据中的异常。

senses.title: A genetic or chromosomal defect
senses.definition: an alteration in genes or chromosomes that departs from the typical pattern
senses.definitionCN: 基因或染色体上偏离典型模式的改变
senses.example: The clinic screens for chromosomal abnormalities before birth.
senses.exampleCN: 诊所在出生前筛查染色体异常。
senses.why: The blueprint has a standard form; a change in that form is the most literal kind of abnormality.
senses.whyCN: 蓝图有标准形态；这一形态发生改变，就是最本义的异常。

senses.title: A structural defect in materials
senses.definition: an irregularity in the structure of a material or object that may weaken it
senses.definitionCN: 材料或物件结构上的不规则，可能使其强度下降
senses.example: Inspectors found an abnormality in the weld.
senses.exampleCN: 检验员发现焊缝处有一处结构异常。
senses.why: The square measures metal as it measures bodies: a place that will not line up is a defect.
senses.whyCN: 曲尺量金属和量身体一样：对不齐的地方就是缺陷。

senses.title: A rare or strange occurrence
senses.definition: an event or thing that is so unusual that it stands out from ordinary experience
senses.definitionCN: 罕见到足以从日常经验中凸显出来的事件或事物
senses.example: The sudden snow in June was called a weather abnormality.
senses.exampleCN: 六月突降大雪被称作天气异常。
senses.why: The countable noun can leave the body and the lab: any departure from the ordinary course can be one.
senses.whyCN: 这个可数名词可以离开身体与实验室：任何偏离寻常进程的事物都能算一处异常。

intro.en: Abnormality is the noun of quality built on abnormal, which in turn rests on the Latin square called norma.
intro.cn: abnormality 是由 abnormal 构成的表性质名词，而 abnormal 又依托拉丁语那把名为 norma 的曲尺。

items.en: Norma was a carpenter's square and, by extension, a rule or standard. Its deeper origin is source uncertain.
items.cn: norma 是木工曲尺，引申为规则与标准；更早的来源不确定。

items.en: Normalis meant according to the square, and English normal developed from it.
items.cn: normalis 意为「按曲尺做成的」，英语 normal 由此发展而来。

items.en: The adjective abnormal appeared in the early nineteenth century, first in scientific and medical writing.
items.cn: 形容词 abnormal 在十九世纪初出现，最初见于科学与医学写作。

items.en: The noun abnormality followed soon after, when writers needed a countable name for specific defects and deviations.
items.cn: 名词 abnormality 紧随其后出现，因为写作者需要一个可数的名称来指具体的缺陷与偏离。

items.en: The word now covers medicine, genetics, engineering and statistics, wherever a baseline can be drawn.
items.cn: 如今这个词覆盖医学、遗传学、工程与统计，凡能画出基线的领域都可使用。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the norm- family; the near-meaning group gathers nouns for defects and deviations.
note.cn: 形近组收 norm- 词族；近义组收表示缺陷与偏离的名词。

entries.definition: A departure from a regular pattern or rule.

entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「偏离、偏差」，强调与预期路线或数值的差距。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real norma root and the medical and technical phrases the word appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子使用真实的 norma 词根，以及这个词实际出现的医学与技术搭配。

normal.en: Norma is the square, so an abnormality is a place that will not square up.
normal.cn: norma 是曲尺，abnormality 就是一处对不上尺的地方。

normal.en: Abnormal is the adjective, abnormality the countable thing it points at.
normal.cn: abnormal 是形容词，abnormality 是它指出的那个可数事物。

normal.en: A congenital abnormality is one present from birth, before any habit could form.
normal.cn: congenital abnormality 指出生就有的异常，习惯还来不及形成。

normal.en: Chromosomal abnormality moves the image to the blueprint of the body.
normal.cn: chromosomal abnormality 把意象移到身体的那张蓝图上。

normal.en: Inspectors look for structural abnormalities in welds and bones alike.
normal.cn: 检验员在焊缝和骨骼里找的都是结构异常。

abstract.cn: 想象一面整齐的砖墙里有一块砖歪了：目光会停在那里。

abstract.en: The tilted brick can be in a body, a gene, a weld or a data table.
abstract.cn: 这块歪砖可以出现在身体、基因、焊缝或数据表里。

abstract.en: Abnormality is countable: each departure gets its own name in a report.
abstract.cn: abnormality 是可数的：报告里每一处偏离都有自己的名字。

examples.en: The scan detected an abnormality near the joint.
examples.cn: 扫描在关节附近发现一处异常。

examples.en: Doctors monitor children for growth abnormalities.
examples.cn: 医生监测儿童是否存在发育异常。

examples.en: There was no abnormality in the final inspection.
examples.cn: 最终检验中没有发现异常。

sensesIntro.en: The eight senses of abnormality all give a name to one place where something refuses to line up: a state, a body part, a test value, behaviour, data, genes, a material, or a rare event.
sensesIntro.cn: abnormality 的八个义项都在为某一处「对不上线」命名：状态、身体部位、检查数值、行为、数据、基因、材料，或罕见事件。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one tilted brick stands out in a wall of straight ones.
core.cn: 核心意象：一排笔直的砖里，一块歪砖格外显眼。

branches.en: THE STATE: the bare quality of departing from the standard.
branches.cn: 状态线：偏离标准的性质本身。

branches.en: THE BODY: a malformation or a genetic change names the defect in the flesh.
branches.cn: 身体线：畸形或基因改变为肉体上的缺陷命名。

branches.en: THE READING: test values and data points that fall outside the range.
branches.cn: 读数线：落在范围之外的检查值与数据点。

branches.en: THE OUTSIDE WORLD: behaviour and rare events are judged against expectation.
branches.cn: 外部世界线：行为与罕见事件要对照预期来评判。

branches.en: THE MATERIAL: a weld or structure that will not square up is a defect.
branches.cn: 材料线：对不上尺的焊缝或结构就是缺陷。

senses.title: Things tied in one package
senses.definition: a number of things tied or wrapped together
senses.definitionCN: 若干东西被扎或包在一起
senses.example: He carried a bundle of newspapers to the door.
senses.exampleCN: 他抱着一捆报纸走到门口。
senses.why: This is the oldest sense, from a word for binding.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老的义项，来自表示「捆扎」的词。

senses.title: To tie things together

senses.title: To sell things as one package

senses.why: A bundle of goods is sold as one item, and the verb followed.

definition_zh: 剂量；一剂；一次（不愉快的经历）；给药
definition_en: a measured amount of medicine taken at one time, an amount of something experienced, or to give medicine to someone
core_image: 一只量杯对着标签上的刻度，护士仔细核对
scene: 药瓶上贴着模糊的标签，护士拿量杯仔细对了一遍刻度。 The label warns patients not to exceed the daily dose.
sceneCN: 这里 dose 是「剂量」（第 1 个义项：一次服用的、经过计量的药量）；句意是标签警告病人不要超过每日剂量。

pos.zh: 名词：剂量；一剂；一次（不愉快的经历）

derivatives.zh: 由本词加名词后缀 -age 构成，义为「用量；剂量」

senses.title: A measured amount of medicine
senses.definition: a measured amount of a medicine or drug taken at one time

senses.example: The doctor reduced the dose after the first week.
senses.exampleCN: 第一周之后医生减少了剂量。
senses.why: Greek dosis meant a giving, and medicine turned that giving into an exact quantity measured out for one occasion.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 dosis 意为「给予」，医学把这次给予变成一次称量好的精确数量。

senses.title: An unpleasant experience
senses.definition: an amount of something unpleasant that a person has to experience, such as an illness or a shock
senses.definitionCN: 一个人不得不承受的某种不快之物的分量，如疾病或惊吓
senses.example: He got a dose of flu during the trip.
senses.exampleCN: 旅途中他得了一次流感。
senses.why: If medicine comes in doses, then anything that hits the body or the feelings can also arrive in one measured portion.
senses.whyCN: 既然药可以按剂来算，那么任何冲击身体或情绪的东西也能以一份计量好的分量到来。

senses.title: To give medicine to
senses.definition: to give a person or animal a measured amount of medicine or another substance
senses.definitionCN: 给一个人或动物服用一定量的药或其他物质
senses.example: The farmer dosed the sick calf with a bitter liquid.
senses.exampleCN: 农夫给病牛犊喂了一种苦味的药水。
senses.why: The noun became a verb: to dose is to hand over exactly the measured giving the noun names.
senses.whyCN: 名词变成动词：dose 就是把名词所指的那份计量好的给予交出去。

examples.cn: 随餐服用这一剂，以免胃痛。

examples.en: The nurse dosed the child every six hours.
examples.cn: 护士每六小时给孩子服一次药。

examples.en: The trip gave him a dose of cold wind and hard truth.
examples.cn: 这趟旅程给了他一阵冷风和一次现实的教训。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「抖死」——剂量过大真会让人抖得厉害；所以 dose 要按刻度来。

root: 源自希腊语 dosis（给予），由 didonai（给）派生，经晚期拉丁语 dosis 与法语 dose 进入英语。本义是「给出的一份」，医学上固定为一次计量好的药量，后又引申指一次不愉快的经历，并产生动词「给药」义。

sensesIntro.en: One giving word measures medicine, measures bad experiences, and finally names the act of giving medicine.
sensesIntro.cn: 同一个「给」的词，既计量药，也计量糟糕的经历，最后还指给药这个动作。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a small measuring cup aligned with the marks on a bottle label.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只小量杯对准药瓶标签上的刻度。

branches.en: MEDICINE: the first sense is the exact amount of a drug taken at one time.
branches.cn: 药物线：第一个义项是一次服用的精确药量。

branches.en: EXPERIENCE: the second sense measures illness or shock instead of medicine.
branches.cn: 经历线：第二个义项计量的不是药，而是疾病或冲击。

branches.en: THE ACTION: the third sense is the handing over of that measured amount.
branches.cn: 动作线：第三个义项是把那份计量好的量交出去。

branches.en: The noun and verb face each other: the dose is what the act of dosing delivers.
branches.cn: 名词与动词相对：dose 就是给药动作所交付的东西。

branches.en: Medicine and misfortune both arrive in portions one has to take.
branches.cn: 药与不幸都以人必须承受的一份份分量到来。

intro.en: Dose is a Greek-derived stem; English adds -age, -meter and over- to build its family.
intro.cn: dose 是源自希腊语的词干，英语靠 -age、-meter 与 over- 扩展词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin borrowed dosis from Greek, so the Latin entry is itself a loan word.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 dosis 借自希腊语，因此这条拉丁条目本身也是借词。

items.example: The Greek verb is the giving root.
items.exampleCN: 这个希腊动词是「给」的词根。

items.example: Greek doctors used it for medicine.
The dose is printed on the box.
The dosage depends on body weight.

latinEntries.structure: Late Latin noun, borrowed from Greek
latinEntries.meaning: a giving, a portion of medicine

derivatives.zh: 由本词加名词后缀 -age 构成，义为「用量；剂量」
由 dose 加 -meter「测量器」构成，义为「剂量计」
由前缀 over-「过量」加本词构成，义为「用药过量；服药过量」

definition_zh: 驾驶；掌舵；引导
definition_en: to control the direction of a vehicle, a ship, or a course of action
core_image: 一只手稳稳握住方向盘
scene: 他小心地把船驶过礁石。 He steered the boat carefully past the rocks.
sceneCN: 这里 steer 是「驾驶、掌舵」（第 1 个义项）；句意：他小心地把船驶过礁石。

derivatives.zh: 转向装置；操纵
舵手
统舱；驾驶

senses.title: Control direction
senses.definition: to control the direction in which a vehicle moves
senses.definitionCN: 控制车辆行进的方向
senses.example: He steered the boat carefully past the rocks.
senses.exampleCN: 他小心地把船驶过礁石。
senses.why: This is the hands-on driving sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是双手操作的驾驶义项。

senses.title: Guide a course
senses.definition: to guide a plan, a discussion, or a group in a direction
senses.definitionCN: 引导计划、讨论或群体朝某方向走
senses.example: She steered the talk back to the main point.
senses.exampleCN: 她把谈话引回要点。
senses.why: A wheel controls a ship, and a hand can control a talk.
senses.whyCN: 方向盘操纵船，手也能操纵谈话。

senses.title: Keep a heading
senses.definition: to keep a ship or aircraft on a chosen course
senses.definitionCN: 使船或飞机保持选定的航向
senses.example: Steer north until you see the light.
senses.exampleCN: 朝北掌舵，直到看见灯塔。
senses.why: The narrow nautical sense of holding a course.
senses.whyCN: 这是保持航向的航海窄义。

intro.en: Steer comes from Old English steoran, to guide or govern, from a Germanic root.
intro.cn: steer 来自古英语 steoran（引导、治理），源于日耳曼语词根。

items.en: The root meant to guide or direct.
items.cn: 该词根意为引导或指示方向。

items.en: Steoran meant to steer a ship.
items.cn: steoran 意为给船掌舵。

items.en: Steren widened to guiding any vehicle.
items.cn: steren 扩展到驾驶任何交通工具。

items.en: Steer also meant to guide a course of action.
items.cn: steer 也指引导行动方向。

items.en: Steer clear of became a common phrase.
items.cn: steer clear of 成为常用短语。

note.en: Steer is compared with look-alike words and with words for guiding.
note.cn: 把 steer 与形近词以及表示引导的词作比较。

entries.definition: very steep or complete
a hard metal
serious and strict
to operate a vehicle
to show the way
to find and follow a route

normalIntro.en: Steer is a hand on a wheel, then a hand on a conversation, then a ship held to its course.
normalIntro.cn: steer 是握着方向盘的手，是引导谈话的手，也是把船稳在航线上的手。

normal.en: She steered the car into the lane.
normal.cn: 她把车驶入车道。

normal.en: Steer clear of the broken glass.
normal.cn: 避开碎玻璃。

normal.en: He steered the ship through the storm.
normal.cn: 他驾船穿过风暴。

normal.en: The teacher steered us to the answer.
normal.cn: 老师引导我们找到答案。

normal.en: Steer the bike with both hands.
normal.cn: 双手扶把骑自行车。

abstract.en: Direction is a decision made small, again and again.
abstract.cn: 方向，是一次次微小的决定累积而成。

abstract.en: The hand that steers also chooses what to avoid.
abstract.cn: 掌舵的手，也在选择避开什么。

abstract.en: To guide a talk is to hold a quiet wheel.
abstract.cn: 引导一场谈话，就是握着一只安静的方向盘。

examples.en: He steered the boat carefully past the rocks.
examples.cn: 他小心地把船驶过礁石。

examples.en: She steered the talk back to the main point.
examples.cn: 她把谈话引回要点。

examples.en: Steer clear of the broken glass.
examples.cn: 避开碎玻璃。

dict_mnemonic.text: steer 是「掌舵、驾驶」，也指「引导」；steer clear of 是避开；注意它作名词还可指小公牛，但四级主要考动词义。

root: 来自古英语 steoran（引导、治理），源于日耳曼语；由驾船掌舵，扩展到驾驶车辆、引导谈话与行动。

sensesIntro.en: Steer means to drive a vehicle, to hold a ship to its course, or to guide a course of action.
sensesIntro.cn: steer 指驾驶车辆、稳定航向，或引导行动方向。

core.en: A hand on a wheel deciding a direction.
core.cn: 一只手放在轮上，决定方向。

branches.en: A car turns between two white lines.
branches.cn: 一辆车在两道白线间转向。

branches.en: A voice brings a meeting back to the point.
branches.cn: 一个声音把会议拉回主题。

branches.en: A bow holds steady against the night.
branches.cn: 船首在夜色中稳稳朝前。

branches.en: Driving and sailing are the same grip.
branches.cn: 开车与行船，是同一个握法。

branches.en: A talk needs a wheel as much as a road does.
branches.cn: 谈话和道路一样，都需要一只方向盘。

intro.en: Steer takes verb endings and builds nouns of steering and the steersman.
intro.cn: steer 加动词词尾，并构成表示操纵与舵手的名词。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin root; the word is Germanic.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有拉丁词根，属于日耳曼语来源。

definition_zh: 不合理的；不理智的；过分的；不公道的
definition_en: not fair or sensible, or going beyond what is acceptable
core_image: 有人非要在深夜里把音量调到最大
scene: 邻居把音箱搬到阳台上，说晚上开派对是理所当然的事。 It seems unreasonable to play music so loudly at that hour.
sceneCN: 这里 unreasonable 是「不合理的」（第 1 个义项：讲不通、没道理）；句意为那个钟点把音乐放得那么响实在说不过去。深夜把音量调到最大的画面，正是这个词的核心。

derivatives.zh: 形容词加 -ly 构成副词，义为「不合理地；过度地」
形容词加 -ness 构成名词，义为「不合理；不通情理」
去掉否定前缀后的肯定形式，义为「合理的；讲道理的」
同源名词，义为「理由；理性」
同源名词，义为「推理；论证」

senses.title: Not guided by good sense
senses.definition: not based on good judgement, so that others cannot follow it
senses.definitionCN: 不建立在良好判断之上，别人无法理解
senses.example: It is unreasonable to expect an answer within an hour.
senses.exampleCN: 指望一小时内得到答复是不合情理的。
senses.why: The word is the negative of reasonable, whose base is reason, the power of working things out.
senses.whyCN: 这个词是 reasonable 的反面，而词根 reason 指的正是推想、讲道理的能力。

senses.title: Asking for more than is fair
senses.definition: used of demands or prices that go beyond what is fair
senses.definitionCN: 形容提出过分要求或开出过高价格
senses.example: The hotel charges an unreasonable price for breakfast.
senses.exampleCN: 这家旅馆的早餐要价过高。
senses.why: Once a demand stops following reason, it also stops respecting the fair line, and the excess sense follows.
senses.whyCN: 要求一旦不再讲道理，也就不再顾惜那条公平线，于是「过分」这层意思随之而来。

senses.title: A person who will not listen to sense
senses.definition: used of a person who refuses to be persuaded by argument
senses.definitionCN: 形容听不进道理、怎么劝都没用的人
senses.example: He became unreasonable when anyone mentioned the money.
senses.exampleCN: 谁一提到那笔钱，他就变得不讲道理。
senses.why: When a person cuts himself off from reason, the absence of reason becomes a trait of character.
senses.whyCN: 当一个人把自己和道理隔开，那份「没有道理」就变成了一种性格。

senses.title: Not fair to someone
senses.definition: used of treatment or rules that are unfair to a person
senses.definitionCN: 形容对某人不公平的对待或规矩
senses.example: The rules seem unreasonable to anyone working nights.
senses.exampleCN: 对任何上夜班的人来说，这些规矩都不公道。
senses.why: A rule that no sound reason supports is felt by the people under it as plain injustice.
senses.whyCN: 一条得不到正当理由支撑的规矩，落到受它管的人身上就是明显的不公。

senses.title: Not justified by logic
senses.definition: used of an argument or belief that does not follow from the evidence
senses.definitionCN: 形容论证或信念与证据对不上
senses.example: The conclusion is unreasonable because the evidence does not support it.
senses.exampleCN: 这个结论说不通，因为证据并不支持它。
senses.why: In argument the word narrows to its literal core: the steps of reasoning are missing.
senses.whyCN: 在论证中，这个词收窄到最字面的核心：推理的步骤缺失了。

intro.en: A negative prefix over an adjective built on reason, itself from Latin ratio through French.
intro.cn: 否定前缀压在由 reason 构成的形容词上，而 reason 经法语来自拉丁语 ratio。

items.en: The prefix un- is native and negates adjectives freely.
items.cn: 前缀 un- 为英语本土成分，可自由加在形容词前表示否定。

items.en: Ratio meant reckoning, account, and the faculty of reasoning.
items.cn: ratio 意为「计算、说明」，也指推理的能力。

items.en: Raison carried the same senses of account and judgement into French.
items.cn: raison 把「说明」与「判断」的意思带进法语。

items.en: Reason enters English meaning both a cause given and the mind that gives it.
items.cn: reason 进入英语时兼指「给出的理由」与「给出理由的心智」。

items.en: Reasonable and then unreasonable are formed, and the negative spreads to prices, demands, and people.
items.cn: 先有 reasonable，后有 unreasonable，否定义继而扩展到价格、要求与人。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the reason family, and the near-meaning group collects words of excess and unfairness.
note.cn: 形近组沿 reason 词族展开，近义组汇集表示过分与不公的词。

entries.definition: sensible and fair
in an unfair or excessive way
a cause or the power to judge
the process of thinking things through
so silly that it cannot be believed
far more than is proper
not just or equal
showing good judgement

normalIntro.en: The word is the negative of an adjective everyone learns early, so its parts are plain.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是人人早就会的形容词的否定形式，部件一目了然。

normal.en: Un- plus reasonable: not open to reason at all.
normal.cn: un- 加 reasonable：完全没法讲道理。

normal.en: An unreasonable demand and an unreasonable price are the two fixed collocations.
normal.cn: an unreasonable demand 与 an unreasonable price 是两个固定搭配。

normal.en: The adverb unreasonably often modifies refuse and complain.
normal.cn: 副词 unreasonably 常修饰 refuse 与 complain。

normal.en: Reason, reasonable, and reasoning share the Latin root ratio.
normal.cn: reason、reasonable、reasoning 共享拉丁词根 ratio。

normal.en: Legal English uses unreasonable of terms that no fair person would accept.
normal.cn: 法律英语里 unreasonable 指任何通情达理的人都不会接受的条件。

abstract.en: Hear loud music from a balcony long after midnight.
abstract.cn: 在过了午夜很久之后听见阳台上传来很响的音乐。

abstract.en: See a customer shout at a clerk over a coin.
abstract.cn: 看见有人为一枚硬币对店员大喊。

abstract.en: Feel your hand stop moving on a clock that will not agree.
abstract.cn: 感受你的手停在一只怎么也对不上的钟上。

examples.en: It is unreasonable to blame the driver for a delay he cannot control.
examples.cn: 把司机控制不了的延误怪在他头上是不合情理的。

examples.en: The shop was criticised for charging unreasonable prices during the festival.
examples.cn: 这家店因节日期间要价过高而受到批评。

examples.en: She refused to argue with a friend who had become unreasonable.
examples.cn: 她拒绝再跟一个已经听不进道理的朋友争论。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「俺不理事儿」——别人摆事实讲道理，俺不理那套，这种做法自然就显得不合理。

root: 英语本土构词：前缀 un-（不）+ reasonable（合理的），reasonable 由 reason 加 -able 构成，reason 源自拉丁语 ratio（计算、理性）经古法语 raison 进入英语

sensesIntro.en: One root idea, showing no trace of reason, branches into outrage, resistance, unfair treatment, and weak proof.
sensesIntro.cn: 一个根义「看不到道理」，分出过火、倔强、不公与推理站不住四路。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand turning the volume knob to its limit.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手把音量旋钮拧到最顶。

branches.en: The logic branch: a request no sound mind could follow.
branches.cn: 事理分支：清醒的人都跟不上的要求。

branches.en: The excess branch: prices and demands past the fair line.
branches.cn: 过度分支：越过公平线的价格与要求。

branches.en: The person branch: a friend who stops listening.
branches.cn: 人物分支：一个不再听劝的朋友。

branches.en: The fairness branch: treatment that singles someone out.
branches.cn: 公平分支：只针对某人的对待。

branches.en: The argument branch: a conclusion that does not follow.
branches.cn: 论证分支：推不出来的结论。

intro.en: A native negative prefix and a word-forming suffix sit on the ordinary noun for reason.
intro.cn: 本土否定前缀与构词后缀都压在日常名词 reason 上。

latinIntro.en: The Latin source is ratio, reckoning, with the verb reri behind it, to think or suppose.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁来源是 ratio（计算），其后的动词 reri 意为「思考、推想」。

items.example: He gave no reason for leaving.
items.exampleCN: 他没有给出离开的理由。

items.meaningCN: 表示状态或性质的名词后缀

items.example: He objected unreasonably to every plan.
items.exampleCN: 他对每个计划都不讲道理地反对。
她给出了有理有据的回答。

definition_zh: 装备；配备；使有能力
definition_en: to supply someone or something with the tools or skills needed
core_image: 出发前把工具一件件装进背包
scene: 学校为每间实验室配备了新的显微镜。 The school equipped every lab with new microscopes.
sceneCN: 这里 equipped 是 equip 的过去式，表示「配备」（第 1 个义项：提供所需的工具或设备）；句意：学校为每间实验室配备了新的显微镜。

derivatives.zh: 设备；装备
装备好的；有能力的

senses.title: To supply with tools or gear
senses.definition: to provide a person or place with the tools, machines, or gear needed
senses.definitionCN: 为某人或某地提供所需的工具、机器或装备
senses.example: The team was equipped with maps and radios.
senses.exampleCN: 队伍配备了地图和无线电。
senses.why: The word came from fitting out a ship, so the basic sense is supplying the necessary gear.
senses.whyCN: 这个词原指为船只配备物资，因此基本含义是提供必需的装备。

senses.title: To prepare someone with skills
senses.definition: to give someone the knowledge or skills needed for a task
senses.definitionCN: 给予某人完成任务所需的知识或技能
senses.example: The course equips students to work in hospitals.
senses.exampleCN: 这门课程使学生有能力在医院工作。
senses.why: Equipment can be mental as well as physical, so the verb extends to training.
senses.whyCN: 装备既可以是物质的，也可以是头脑中的，所以动词扩展到培训。

senses.title: To fit out a place
senses.definition: to furnish a room, building, or vehicle with what it needs
senses.definitionCN: 为房间、建筑或车辆配置所需设备
senses.example: They equipped the new kitchen with modern appliances.
senses.exampleCN: 他们为新厨房配置了现代电器。
senses.why: The same supplying action applies to places and vehicles, not only to people.
senses.whyCN: 同样的供给动作也适用于场所和车辆，而不只是人。

intro.en: Equip comes from Old French esquiper, to fit out a ship, probably from a Germanic word for ship.
intro.cn: equip 来自古法语 esquiper（为船只配备物资），可能源于日耳曼语中表示「船」的词。

items.en: A Germanic skip word means ship.
items.cn: 日耳曼语中 skip 一词意为船。

items.en: Esquiper means to fit out a ship.
items.cn: esquiper 意为为船只配备物资。

items.en: The word extends to fitting out a person or army.
items.cn: 这个词扩展到为个人或军队配备。

items.en: Equip enters English with the gear sense.
items.cn: equip 以「装备」的含义进入英语。

items.en: Modern English adds the sense of preparing with skills.
items.cn: 现代英语增加了「以技能作准备」的含义。

note.en: Equip is a supplying verb, closely tied to equipment and to words for furnishing.
note.cn: equip 是表示供给的动词，与 equipment 以及表示配置的词关系紧密。

entries.definition: the tools and gear needed
having the needed gear
the act of supplying gear
to supply a room with furniture
to provide what is needed
to supply with weapons

normalIntro.en: Equip began as fitting out a ship; now you can equip a lab, a team, or a student.
normalIntro.cn: equip 最初指为船只配备物资；现在可以为实验室、队伍或学生配备所需。

normal.en: Equip with means supply with.
normal.cn: equip with 表示配备。

normal.en: A fully equipped kitchen has every tool you need.
normal.cn: fully equipped 的厨房拥有你需要的每样工具。

normal.en: The noun equipment is uncountable.
normal.cn: 名词 equipment 是不可数名词。

normal.en: A course can equip you for a career.
normal.cn: 一门课程可以让你有能力从事某种职业。

normal.en: Compare supply: supply is broader, equip stresses gear or preparation.
normal.cn: 对比 supply：supply 更宽泛，equip 强调装备或准备。

abstract.en: Picture a sailor loading ropes and lanterns onto a ship.
abstract.cn: 想象水手把绳索和灯笼装上船。

abstract.en: Imagine a hiker checking each item in a backpack.
abstract.cn: 想象徒步者逐一检查背包里的物品。

abstract.en: Think of a student leaving a class with a new skill.
abstract.cn: 想象一名学生带着新技能走出课堂。

examples.en: Rescue teams were equipped with warm clothing.
examples.cn: 救援队配备了保暖衣物。

examples.en: The training equips nurses to handle emergencies.
examples.cn: 这项培训使护士有能力处理紧急情况。

examples.en: They equipped the office with new computers.
examples.cn: 他们为办公室配备了新电脑。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「e + quip」——出发前把工具「配齐」，就是装备；这只是拆词联想，与词源无关。

root: 古法语 esquiper（为船只配备物资）→ 中古英语 equip，核心义「把所需之物配齐」，引申为使有能力。

sensesIntro.en: Equip starts with supplying gear, extends to preparing people with skills, and applies to fitting out places.
sensesIntro.cn: equip 从提供装备开始，扩展到以技能培养人，并适用于为场所配置设备。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a backpack filled with every tool the trip needs.
core.cn: 核心意象：背包里装满旅途所需的每样工具。

branches.en: Supplying tools is the basic physical sense.
branches.cn: 提供工具是基本的物质义项。

branches.en: Supplying skills extends gear to the mind.
branches.cn: 提供技能把装备扩展到头脑。

branches.en: Fitting out a place applies the same action to rooms.
branches.cn: 为场所配置设备把同一动作用于房间。

branches.en: A lab and a hiker are both fitted out with gear.
branches.cn: 实验室与徒步者都被配齐了装备。

branches.en: Both tools and training prepare someone for a task.
branches.cn: 工具与培训都让人为任务做好准备。

intro.en: Equip is a French fitting-out verb, with English equipment and equipped built from it.
intro.cn: equip 是法语中表示「配备」的动词，英语由它构成 equipment 与 equipped。

latinIntro.en: The French esquiper, to fit out a ship, probably comes from a Germanic word for ship.
latinIntro.cn: 法语 esquiper（为船只配备）可能来自日耳曼语中表示「船」的词。

items.example: Skip is the probable ship root.
items.exampleCN: skip 是可能表示「船」的词根。

items.example: Esquiper starts as a sailing word.

items.meaning: forming a past form or adjective

items.exampleCN: equipped 描述准备好的状态。
equipping 指正在进行的动作。
fully 常与 equipped 搭配。

definition_zh: 多个的；不止一个的；多种的；倍数
definition_en: made up of more than one part, person or element; involving several different kinds; and, as a noun, a number that another number contains an exact number of times
core_image: 同一盏灯被几面镜子映出一排一模一样的光点，一个光源变成许多个
scene: 地下车库里并排划出许多相同的车位，墙面刷着重复的编号，管理方说这是为了方便不同楼层的住户。 The new block has multiple entrances so that people can reach the shops from several sides.
sceneCN: 这里是「多个的、不止一个的」（第 1 个义项：由不止一个部分或个体构成）；句意为这栋新楼开了好几个入口，人们可以从不同方向走到商店。图中可辨识物件：重复的编号、并排的车位、几处入口。

pos.zh: 多个的；不止一个的；多种的

derivatives.zh: 由 multiple 的词干加 -ply（折）构成，义为「乘；成倍增加」
由 multiply 加名词后缀 -ation 构成，义为「乘法；增多」
由拉丁语 multus（多）加 -tude 构成，义为「大量；众多」
由前缀 multi-（多）与 cultural 复合而成，义为「多元文化的」

senses.title: Consisting of more than one part or person
senses.definition: made up of more than one person, thing or part, rather than a single one
senses.definitionCN: 由不止一个人、事物或部分构成，而不是只有一个
senses.example: The patient was given multiple tests before the diagnosis.
senses.exampleCN: 在确诊之前，病人接受了多项检查。
senses.why: Latin multus gave the first element its sense of many, and -plex says fold, so the word pictures one thing folded over several times instead of a single piece.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 multus 给这个词的前半部分带来「多」的意思，-plex 表示「折」，所以它的画面是同一件东西叠了好几层，而不是单独一份。

senses.title: Having many different kinds
senses.definition: involving several different types, causes or aspects rather than just one
senses.definitionCN: 涉及若干不同的类型、原因或方面，而不只是单一的
senses.example: The report lists multiple causes for the drop in sales.
senses.exampleCN: 报告列出了销量下滑的多种原因。
senses.why: Once -plex can count the folds, it can count the kinds as well: several types laid side by side become multiple causes, a multiple problem or multiple meanings.
senses.whyCN: 既然 -plex 能数「折了几层」，它也就能数「有几种」：几种类型平铺在一起，就成了多种原因、多重问题或多重含义。

senses.title: A number contained exactly in another
senses.definition: a number that another number contains an exact number of times, as four is a multiple of two
senses.definitionCN: 能被另一个数整除的数，例如四是二的倍数
senses.example: Twelve is a multiple of three and of four.
senses.exampleCN: 十二是三和四的倍数。
senses.why: The mathematical sense keeps the picture of repeated folds: a multiple is a small unit folded over an exact number of times, with nothing left outside the count.
senses.whyCN: 数学义保留「一折再折」的画面：一个倍数就是小单位被完整地叠上若干次，一点零头都不剩。

intro.en: Multiple joins two Latin pieces, multus for many and -plex for folded, and it entered English through French as a word for what is manifold.
intro.cn: multiple 由两个拉丁成分合成：multus 意为「多」，-plex 意为「折、编织」；它经法语进入英语，指多重的东西。

items.en: Multus meant many or much and supplied the first half of a large family of counting words.
items.cn: multus 意为「多、许多」，为一大族计数词提供了前半部分。

items.en: -Plex came from plectere, to fold or weave, and it described something with a stated number of folds, as in duplex and triplex.
items.cn: -plex 出自 plectere（折、编织），描述具有特定折数的事物，如 duplex 与 triplex。

items.en: Multiplex joined the two pieces: many folds, and therefore manifold, having many parts or forms.
items.cn: multiplex 把两者合起来：许多折，因此是多样的，包含许多部分或形式。

items.en: French took multiplex as multiple and used it for what is composed of several elements rather than one.
items.cn: 法语把 multiplex 写作 multiple，用来指由若干成分而非单一成分构成的事物。

items.en: English borrowed the adjective in the seventeenth century, later making it a noun for a multiple in arithmetic and for repeated bus or train services.
items.cn: 英语在十七世纪借入这个形容词，后来又把它用作名词，指算术中的倍数，也指重复开行的公交班次。

note.en: The look-alike group collects words built on the Latin elements for many and folds; the near-meaning group collects words for several parts and exact divisibility.
note.cn: 形近组收由拉丁语「多」与「折」两个成分构成的词；近义组收表示若干部分与整除关系的词。

entries.definition: To increase in number, or to perform the operation of multiplication.
entries.definitionCN: 增加数量，或进行乘法运算。

entries.definition: The arithmetic operation of combining equal groups, or the act of increasing greatly.
entries.definitionCN: 把若干相等的组成合起来的算术运算，或大幅增多。

entries.definition: A very large number of people or things.
Having two parts or two dwellings joined together; the -plex element is the same.
entries.definitionCN: 由两个部分或两所住宅相连而成；其中的 -plex 成分相同。

entries.definition: More than two but not very many.
Of several different kinds.
Great in number; many.
Of many kinds or forms; also a fitting with several branches.
entries.definitionCN: 许多种类或形式的；也指多支管的接头。

normalIntro.en: The word is two Latin pieces, many plus fold, and every sense is a different way of counting repetitions.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词就是两个拉丁成分：多与折；每个义项都是数「重复了几次」的不同方式。

normal.en: Multus is Latin for many, so multiple starts from a plain count of more than one.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 multus 意为多，所以 multiple 的起点就是「不止一个」这个简单的计数。

normal.en: -Plex comes from folding, and duplex, triplex and multiplex all count how many folds a thing has.
normal.cn: -plex 出自「折」，duplex、triplex、multiplex 都在数一样东西折了几层。

normal.en: A multiple in arithmetic keeps that fold image: one number is folded into another an exact number of times.
normal.cn: 算术里的倍数保留了这个折叠画面：一个数被另一个数完整地叠进若干次。

normal.en: Multiply is the verb of the same family, which shows that the word is about making counts grow.
normal.cn: multiply 是同族的动词，说明这个词关心的是让数量长大。

normal.en: Multiple choice counts the options set side by side, which is why it names a test with several answers.
normal.cn: multiple choice 数的是并排摆出的几个选项，所以它指有几项答案的选择题。

abstract.en: Picture one lamp reflected in a row of mirrors, each image the same yet separately present.
abstract.cn: 想象一盏灯被一面面镜子照出一排光点，每个映像都一样，却又各自存在。

abstract.en: A multiple is not a vague many but a countable repetition, so the word always implies a number of parts.
abstract.cn: multiple 不是笼统的「多」，而是可以数清的重复，所以它总含着「若干份」的意思。

abstract.en: When a report blames multiple causes, it says that no single cause can carry the whole story.
abstract.cn: 当报告归因于 multiple causes，它其实是在说：没有任何一个原因能独自解释全部。

examples.en: The new block has multiple entrances so that people can reach the shops from several sides.
examples.cn: 这栋新楼开了好几个入口，人们可以从不同方向走到商店。

examples.en: She checked the figures multiple times before signing the report.
examples.cn: 签字之前，她把数字核对了好几遍。

examples.en: Eight is a multiple of four.
examples.cn: 八是四的倍数。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「马替坡」——一匹马替几拨人爬坡，来回好几趟；记住 multiple 是多个的、多重、倍数。

root: 拉丁语 multus（多）加 -plex（折，出自 plectere 折、编织）构成 multiplex，经法语 multiple 进入英语；同族词有 multiply、multiplication、multitude、duplex 等。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a count of more than one; the senses divide into a number of parts, a number of kinds, and exact divisibility in arithmetic.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「不止一个」的计数；义项分出若干部分、若干种类，以及算术中的整除关系。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a single lamp reflected in a row of mirrors, one source appearing many times.
core.cn: 核心意象：一盏灯被一排镜子照出许多光点，一个光源重复出现。

branches.en: a doorway repeated along a wall so a crowd can spread out
branches.cn: 同一扇门在墙上重复几次，让人群分流

branches.en: one job split among several pairs of hands
branches.cn: 一件活分到好几双手上

branches.en: a list of reasons that no single cause could explain
branches.cn: 一张罗列多种原因的清单，单一原因解释不了

branches.en: a number fitting into another with nothing left over
branches.cn: 一个数正好嵌进另一个数，一点不剩

branches.en: a count that is repeated rather than merely large
branches.cn: 不是笼统地多，而是可以数清的重复

intro.en: Two Latin pieces, many and folded, plus the English words built from them hold the entry together.
intro.cn: 两个拉丁成分「多」与「折」，以及由它们构成的英语词，把这个词条撑了起来。

latinIntro.en: Latin supplies both halves of the word: multus for many and -plex for folds, and multiplex is the source adjective.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语提供了这个词的两半：multus 表示多，-plex 表示折，而 multiplex 就是来源形容词。

definition_zh: 第十三；第十三的；十三分之一
definition_en: coming after twelve others in order, or one of thirteen equal parts
core_image: 第十三级台阶：踩上去之前,你已数过十二级
scene: 旧旅馆的电梯键从十二跳到十四,只剩楼梯忠实如一。 He climbed to the thirteenth floor by the stairs.
sceneCN: 这里 thirteenth 是「第十三」（第 1 个义项：排序中的位置）；句意：他走楼梯上了第十三层。

derivatives.zh: 十三（thirteenth 的基数词基础）
第三十（形近序数词，属 thirty 一族）
第十二（-teenth 序数词族的前一位）
第十三（罕见列举用法，极少使用）

senses.title: Position after twelve
senses.definition: coming after twelve other people or things in order
senses.definitionCN: 按顺序排在另外十二个之后
senses.example: Her office is on the thirteenth floor.
senses.exampleCN: 她的办公室在第十三层。
senses.why: The ordinal pins the number to a place in the line: not thirteen of them, but the one at position thirteen.
senses.whyCN: 序数词把数字钉在线上的一个位置：不是十三个，而是第十三位的那一个。

senses.title: A date: the thirteenth day
senses.titleCN: 十三日：每月的第十三天
senses.definition: the thirteenth day of a month
senses.definitionCN: 一个月中的第十三天
senses.example: The lease begins on the thirteenth of May.
senses.exampleCN: 租约从五月十三日开始。
senses.why: Calendars are queues of days, and the ordinal names your place in the month's line.
senses.whyCN: 日历就是日子的队列，序数词标出你在月份长队中的位置。

senses.title: One of thirteen equal parts
senses.definition: one of thirteen equal parts of a whole
senses.definitionCN: 整体十三等分后的一份
senses.example: Each heir received a thirteenth of the estate.
senses.exampleCN: 每位继承人得到遗产的十三分之一。
senses.why: Cut the whole into thirteen and each slice inherits the ordinal's name, as with third and fourth.
senses.whyCN: 把整体切成十三份，每份便继承序数词之名，如 third、fourth 一般。

intro.en: Thirteenth is thirteen wearing the old ordinal ending -th, a suffix so ancient that it already worked on number words in the first Germanic songs.
intro.cn: thirteenth 就是 thirteen 加上古老的序数后缀 -th；这个后缀极其古老，在最早的日耳曼歌谣里就已作用于数词。

items.en: Germanic built ordinals with a -tha (or -da) ending on the number stem, a habit kept across all the daughter languages.
items.cn: 日耳曼语在数词词干上加 -tha (or -da) 构成序数词，这一习惯在各支语言中保留至今。

items.en: Old English Threoteotha (or Threoteotha) joined the teen number with the ordinal ending.
items.cn: 古英语 Threoteotha 把 -teen 数词与序数后缀连成一体。

items.en: Middle English Threttenthe (or Threttenthe) followed the settled form of thirteen and added the simplified -th.
items.cn: 中古英语 Threttenthe 在 thirteen 的定型形式上加简化后的 -th。

items.en: Modern English fixed thirteenth, the heaviest mouthful among the teens, with 13th as the friendly short form.
items.cn: 现代英语定型 thirteenth——-teen 数词中最拗口的一个——缩写 13th 更为顺口。

items.en: The date sense spread with printed calendars, where the thirteenth of the month carried its unlucky folklore.
items.cn: 随印刷日历普及，日期义传播开来，每月十三号也背上了不吉的民俗。

note.en: The first group lines up the ordinal against its base and neighbours; the second gathers the century and date companions.
note.cn: 第一组将序数词与其基数及相邻序数并列；第二组是世纪与日期中的同伴。

entries.definition: the cardinal; thirteenth is its ordinal partner
entries.definitionCN: 基数词十三；thirteenth 是它的序数搭档

entries.definition: the ordinal of thirty; one syllable apart but a different decade
entries.definitionCN: 第三十；与 thirteenth 仅差一个音节，却差了一代人

entries.definition: position twelve, the step just below
coming at the end of a known series
entries.definitionCN: 最后的；已知序列中的末位

entries.definition: second to last in a series
the fear of the number thirteen
entries.definitionCN: 十三恐惧症；对数字十三的恐惧

normalIntro.en: Real hooks: the old -th ending, the teen stress kept intact, and the calendar job.
normalIntro.cn: 真实联系：古老的 -th 后缀、保留的 teen 重音、以及日历职能。

normal.en: Thirteenth = thirteen + th: the ordinal takes the base and pins it to a place.
normal.cn: thirteenth = thirteen + th：序数词把基数钉在位置上。

normal.en: Keep the teen stress: thirTEENTH.
normal.cn: 重音仍在 teen：thirTEENTH。

normal.en: Careful: thirteenth is 13th, thirtieth is 30th.
normal.cn: 小心区分：thirteenth 是 13th，thirtieth 是 30th。

normal.en: The thirteenth century runs the 1200s, not the 1300s.
normal.cn: 十三世纪指 1200 年代，而非 1300 年代。

normal.en: A thirteenth share: the whole cut into thirteen.
normal.cn: a thirteenth share：整体切成十三份。

abstract.en: An ordinal is a number with an address.
abstract.cn: 序数词是带着门牌号的数字。

abstract.en: The thirteenth step is only unlucky before you climb it.
abstract.cn: 第十三级台阶只有在你踏上之前才不吉利。

abstract.en: Calendars are queues; ordinals hand out the tickets.
abstract.cn: 日历是长队，序数词负责发号。

examples.en: The thirteenth of March was cold and clear.
examples.cn: 三月十三日又冷又晴。

examples.en: This bridge was built in the thirteenth century.
examples.cn: 这座桥建于十三世纪。

examples.en: She finished thirteenth in the marathon.
examples.cn: 她在马拉松中获得第十三名。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「瑟提恩斯」——数到第十三下,「瑟」得牙齿都「斯斯」响 → thirteenth 第十三

root: thirteen「十三」+ 古日耳曼序数后缀 -th（古英语 -tha）→ 古英语 Threoteotha → 中古英语定型；-th 后缀与 first、second 系统并行，是英语最古老的构词法之一。

sensesIntro.en: Thirteenth pins thirteen to a position in a line, to a day of the month, and to one slice of a whole cut into thirteen.
sensesIntro.cn: thirteenth 把十三钉在序列位置、月中的日子，以及整体十三等分的一份上。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a number wearing an address tag.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个戴着门牌号的数字。

branches.en: The rank in a queue of twelve before you.
branches.cn: 身前还有十二人的名次。

branches.en: The day the month hands you its unluckiest ticket.
branches.cn: 月份发出的最不吉利的一张号牌。

branches.en: The slice of a whole cut thirteen ways.
branches.cn: 整体十三等分的一份。

branches.en: Both are the calendar face of the ordinal.
branches.cn: 两者都是序数词的日历面孔。

branches.en: Fractions borrow the ordinal as a name.
branches.cn: 分数借用序数词作名字。

intro.en: Thirteenth shows the Germanic ordinal builder -th at work on a teen number.
intro.cn: thirteenth 展示日耳曼序数构造成分 -th 作用于 -teen 数词。

latinIntro.en: No Latin source; the ordinal system is native, so the Latin entry list stays empty.
latinIntro.cn: 没有拉丁语来源；序数体系为本土，拉丁词条留空。

items.meaningCN: 使数字表示位置（序数后缀）
items.example: Four, fourth; six, sixth; thirteen, thirteenth.
items.exampleCN: four 变 fourth；six 变 sixth；thirteen 变 thirteenth。

items.example: The twelfth round decided the fight.
The twentieth century saw two world wars.
items.exampleCN: 二十世纪经历了两次世界大战。
他们的三十周年结婚纪念日。

items.example: One thirteenth of the crop was lost.
items.exampleCN: 收成的十三分之一损失了。

definition_zh: 居民；住户；（某地的）栖息动物
definition_en: a person or animal that lives in a particular place
core_image: 山脚下几间亮着灯的屋子，每一间里都有人在过日子
scene: 小镇只有一条街，店铺傍晚就早早关门。 Every inhabitant of the island knows the ferry timetable by heart.
sceneCN: 这里 inhabitant 是「居民、住户」（第 1 个义项：居住在某地的人）；句意为岛上的每位居民都把渡船时刻表背得滚瓜烂熟。图中可辨识物件：屋顶、路灯、渡船。

pos.zh: 名词：居民；住户；栖息动物

derivatives.zh: 由本词去掉名词后缀还原，义为「居住于；栖息于」
由动词加过去分词构成，义为「有人居住的」
由动词加否定前缀构成，义为「无人居住的」
由动词加后缀构成，义为「可居住的」

senses.title: A person who lives in a place
senses.definition: a person who lives in a particular town, country, or building
senses.definitionCN: 居住在某个城镇、国家或建筑里的人
senses.example: Most inhabitants of the village work in the fields.
senses.exampleCN: 村里大多数居民在田里干活。
senses.why: In- "in" plus habitare "to dwell" gives a person who dwells inside a place.
senses.whyCN: in-「在内」加 habitare「居住」，得到的就是居住在某地之内的人。

senses.title: An animal that lives somewhere
senses.definition: an animal or plant that lives naturally in a particular area
senses.definitionCN: 在某一地区自然生存的动物或植物
senses.example: Bats are the only inhabitants of the cave in winter.
senses.exampleCN: 冬天蝙蝠是这处洞穴里唯一的栖息者。
senses.why: The same image applies to wild creatures: whoever dwells in a place is its inhabitant.
senses.whyCN: 同一意象也适用于野生生物：凡在某地安身者都是它的 inhabitant。

intro.en: Inhabitant comes from a Latin verb for dwelling, and its ending marks the one who does it.
intro.cn: inhabitant 来自拉丁语表示「居住」的动词，词尾标明动作的承担者。

items.en: Habere meant "to have, hold", and habitare grew from it with the sense "to hold a place, to dwell".
items.cn: habere 意为「拥有、持有」，habitare 由它演变而来，义为「占有某处、居住」。

items.en: The frequentative ending -itare gave habitare its repeated, settled flavour of living somewhere.
items.cn: 表示反复的 -itare 词尾让 habitare 带上「长期待在一处」的意味。

items.en: Old French inhabitant supplied the word to English with the -ant ending of a present participle.
items.cn: 古法语 inhabitant 以现在分词词尾 -ant 把这个词送进英语。

items.en: English adopted it in the late Middle Ages, chiefly in legal and geographical writing.
items.cn: 英语在中世纪晚期采用这个词，主要用于法律与地理文献。

items.en: It now covers animals and plants as easily as people, especially when a habitat is described.
items.cn: 如今它既指人，也常指动植物，尤其在描述栖息地时。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the Latin root of having and dwelling; the near-meaning group gathers words for people who live somewhere.
note.cn: 形近组共享拉丁语「拥有、居住」词根；近义组收表示「住在某地的人」的词。

entries.definition: The natural home of an animal or plant.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「栖息地」，指动植物的天然家园。

entries.definition: The verb meaning to live in a place.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「居住于、栖息于」。

entries.definition: A settled way of behaving, from the same root of holding.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「习惯」，词根同为「持有」。

entries.definition: Someone who lives in a house or area, often formally recorded.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「居民」，多用于正式登记语境。

entries.definition: A legal member of a state, not just someone living there.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「公民」，指法律上的成员，而非仅居住者。

entries.definition: Someone born in a place, rather than merely living there.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「本地人」，强调出生于此。

normalIntro.en: These hooks build on habitare and on the phrases the word usually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子建立在 habitare 与这个词的常见搭配之上。

normal.en: Inhabit is to dwell in: an inhabitant is the one dwelling there.
normal.cn: inhabit 是「住在其中」：inhabitant 就是住在里面的人。

normal.en: Habit, habitat and inhabitant all come from a root meaning to hold.
normal.cn: habit、habitat、inhabitant 都出自表示「持有」的词根。

normal.en: Local inhabitants always know the shortest road.
normal.cn: 本地居民总知道最近的那条路。

normal.en: Writers speak of original inhabitants, meaning those who were there first.
normal.cn: 作者们说 original inhabitants，指最早住在那里的那些人。

normal.en: An uninhabited island has no inhabitants at all.
normal.cn: 无人居住的岛上一个居民也没有。

abstract.en: Picture a house with one lit window: the light is the sign that an inhabitant is inside.
abstract.cn: 想象一栋只亮着一扇窗的房子：那盏灯就是里面有住户的记号。

abstract.en: Inhabitant ties a creature to a place the way a name ties a person to a family.
abstract.cn: inhabitant 把生物与地点连起来，正如名字把人连到家族上。

abstract.en: Every place is defined as much by who dwells there as by what it looks like.
abstract.cn: 一个地方既由它的样子定义，也由住在那里的人定义。

examples.en: The town has fewer than two thousand inhabitants.
examples.cn: 这个镇子居民不到两千人。

examples.en: Foxes are common inhabitants of this forest.
examples.cn: 狐狸是这片森林常见的栖居者。

examples.en: The new road was welcomed by local inhabitants.
examples.cn: 新修的公路受到当地居民欢迎。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「因海比吞」——海边小屋有人住，因海而居成居民

root: 拉丁语 habitare「居住」来自 habere「拥有、持有」，反复词尾 -itare 表示长期待在一处；拉丁现在分词词干 inhabitant- 经古法语进入英语，-ant 标明「做这件事的人」。同根词有 habit、habitat、inhabit。

sensesIntro.en: One dwelling image serves both senses: a person who lives in a place, and an animal that lives there too.
sensesIntro.cn: 两个义项共用同一个「居住」意象：住在某地的人，以及与之为邻的动物。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a house with a single lit window shows that someone dwells inside.
core.cn: 核心意象：一栋只亮着一扇窗的房子说明里面住着人。

branches.en: THE HOUSE: the inhabitant is the one whose daily life fills a dwelling.
branches.cn: 房屋这条线：inhabitant 是日常生活填满一间屋子的那个人。

branches.en: THE TOWN: towns and countries are spoken of as having inhabitants rather than users.
branches.cn: 城镇这条线：说城镇与国家有 inhabitants，而不是使用它们的人。

branches.en: THE WILD: animals and plants are inhabitants of their habitat.
branches.cn: 野生这条线：动植物是它们栖息地的 inhabitants。

branches.en: THE CAVE: the word suits any dweller, including those that never build a house.
branches.cn: 洞穴这条线：这个词适用于任何栖居者，包括从不造房子的那些。

branches.en: THE PLACE: both senses bind a living thing firmly to one spot.
branches.cn: 地点线：两个义项都把生物牢牢绑在某一处。

intro.en: Inhabitant joins a Latin prefix, a Latin root of holding, and a participle ending that names the doer.
intro.cn: inhabitant 由拉丁语前缀、「持有」词根和标明动作承担者的分词词尾合成。

latinIntro.en: Latin habere, habitare and the participle inhabitans are recorded; only the Indo-European root is reconstructed.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 habere、habitare 及分词 inhabitans 均有记录，只有印欧词根属于重构。

items.example: It places the dwelling inside a territory.
items.exampleCN: 它把居住放进某片地域之内。

items.example: The root also gives habit and able.
items.exampleCN: 这一词根还给出 habit 与 able。

items.example: It is the direct source of inhabit.
items.exampleCN: 它是 inhabit 的直接来源。

items.example: It gives the verb its settled, lasting sense.
items.exampleCN: 它让动词带上长久停留的意味。

items.example: It turns the verb into a name for a person.
items.exampleCN: 它把动词变成指人的名词。

items.example: The same root with a different ending.
A negative prefix marks the empty places.
items.exampleCN: 否定前缀标出无人居住之处。

definition_zh: 口音；重音；重音符号；强调
definition_en: the way a group speaks, a stressed syllable, or special emphasis
core_image: 一句话说到某个音节时，声音轻轻往上一挑
scene: 她一张口，尾音轻轻上扬，听得出不是本地人。 His accent told us he had grown up abroad.
sceneCN: 这里的 accent 指「口音」（第 1 个义项：说话带出的地方语音特征）；句意是他的口音表明他在国外长大。

pos.zh: 口音；重音；重音符号；强调

derivatives.zh: 义为「带口音的；重读的」
义为「重音的；按重音节拍的」

senses.title: A way of speaking
senses.definition: the way a group or region pronounces a language
senses.definitionCN: 某一群体或地区说话发音的方式
senses.example: His accent told us he had grown up abroad.
senses.exampleCN: 他的口音表明他在国外长大。
senses.why: The Latin root cantus means song, and accent first named the tune of the voice.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词根 cantus 意为歌唱，accent 最初指嗓音的调子。

senses.title: A stressed syllable
senses.definition: the stronger beat given to one syllable in a word
senses.definitionCN: 一个词中某个音节读得更强
senses.example: The accent falls on the second syllable.
senses.exampleCN: 重音落在第二个音节上。
senses.why: A raised beat in speech is a small song inside a word.
senses.whyCN: 说话时抬高的那一拍，是词里的一小段歌。

senses.title: A written mark
senses.definition: a mark placed over a letter to show its sound
senses.definitionCN: 写在字母上方以标示读音的符号
senses.example: The word carries an accent on the final e.
senses.exampleCN: 这个词最后一个 e 上带一个符号。
senses.why: The tune of the voice was written down as a small mark.
senses.whyCN: 嗓音的调子被写下来，就成了一个小符号。

senses.title: Special emphasis
senses.definition: special importance given to an idea or detail
senses.definitionCN: 给予某个想法或细节的特别重视
senses.example: The report puts the accent on safety.
senses.exampleCN: 这份报告把重点放在安全上。
senses.why: A stressed beat in speech became a stressed point in argument.
senses.whyCN: 言语中加重的一拍，成了论述里被加重的一点。

senses.title: To stress a word
senses.definition: to pronounce a syllable or word more strongly
senses.definitionCN: 把某个音节或词读得更重
senses.example: Accent the first syllable in this name.
senses.exampleCN: 这个名字的第一个音节要重读。
senses.why: The verb simply performs the stress that the noun names.
senses.whyCN: 动词做的，正是名词所指的那一下加重。

intro.en: The word goes back to a Latin noun for song added to speech.
intro.cn: 这个词可追溯到表示「加在言语上的歌」的拉丁名词。

items.en: cantus meant singing or a song.
items.cn: cantus 意为歌唱、歌曲。

items.en: accentus meant a tone added to speech.
items.cn: accentus 指加在言语上的调子。

items.en: accent carried the musical sense into French.
items.cn: accent 把这个音乐性的意义带进法语。

items.en: accent entered English for the tune of the voice.
items.cn: accent 进入英语，指嗓音的调子。

items.en: it now covers regional speech, stress and written marks.
items.cn: 如今它涵盖地方口音、重音与书写符号。

note.en: The look-alike group is the accent family; the near-meaning group is other words about speech sound.
note.cn: 形近组是 accent 词族；近义组是别的与语音有关的词。

normal.en: cantus means song, and accent is the song inside speech.
normal.cn: cantus 意为歌，accent 就是言语里的那点歌。

normal.en: ac- is a form of ad-, meaning added to.
normal.cn: ac- 是 ad- 的变体，意为「加到……上」。

normal.en: a regional accent is a tune learned at home.
normal.cn: 地方口音是在家里学会的调子。

normal.en: a written accent is that tune turned into a mark.
normal.cn: 书写里的重音符号，是那个调子变成了笔画。

normal.en: to accent a point is to make the voice lean on it.
normal.cn: 强调一个观点，就是让声音压在上面。

abstract.en: See a voice rising at the end of a phrase.
abstract.cn: 想象一句话的尾音轻轻上扬。

abstract.en: Picture a small mark floating above a letter.
abstract.cn: 想象字母上方浮着一个小符号。

abstract.en: Think of a finger tapping one beat harder.
abstract.cn: 想象手指在某一拍上敲得更重。

sensesIntro.en: A tune added to speech becomes a regional voice, a stressed beat, a written mark and a point of emphasis.
sensesIntro.cn: 加在言语上的调子，成了地方口音、加重的一拍、纸上的符号，以及被强调的要点。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a voice lifting on one syllable.
core.cn: 核心意象：声音在某个音节上往上一挑。

branches.cn: 一个地方特有的说话方式

branches.cn: 名词的重音与动词的加重

branches.cn: 被写成小符号的调子

intro.cn: 这个词是拉丁前缀加上一个与歌唱有关的词根。

latinIntro.en: The root cantus, song, also gives chant, canticle and incantation.
latinIntro.cn: 词根 cantus（歌）也生出 chant、canticle 与 incantation。

definition_zh: 松树；松木；渴望；憔悴
definition_en: a tall evergreen tree with needle-shaped leaves, its pale soft wood, or to long for someone so much that you grow thin and dull
core_image: 雪坡上一棵针叶树，细长的针叶托着雪，树皮裂成一片片鳞甲
scene: 冬天的山坡上，一排针叶树顶着雪，树皮裂成一片片鳞甲，风穿过细针一样的叶子发出低低的响声。 The old pine at the gate has stood there for a hundred years.
sceneCN: 这里 pine 指「松树」（第 1 个义项：常绿的针叶乔木）；句意为门口那棵老松已经在那里站了一百年。图中可辨识物件：雪坡、针叶、开裂的树皮。

derivatives.zh: 由 pine 加形容词后缀 -y 构成，义为「松树的；松林多的」
由 pine 加表场所的后缀 -ery 构成，义为「松林；松园」
由 pine 加 -ing 构成，义为「苦苦思念；日渐消瘦」

senses.title: An evergreen tree with needle-shaped leaves
senses.definition: a tall evergreen tree with needle-shaped leaves and woody cones that stays green through the winter
senses.definitionCN: 一种高大的常绿乔木，叶如细针，结木质球果，冬季依然青绿
senses.example: An old pine shades the whole yard.
senses.exampleCN: 一棵老松为整个院子遮阴。
senses.why: Latin pinus was simply the name of this tree, and English borrowed the noun together with the tree, so this is the sense the word started from.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 pinus 本来就是这种树的名字，英语连同树一起借来这个名词，所以这是词最原始的义项。

senses.title: The pale soft wood of this tree
senses.definition: the light, soft timber of this tree, used for floors, furniture and paper
senses.definitionCN: 这种树浅色而柔软的木材，用于地板、家具与造纸
senses.example: The floor is made of pine.
senses.exampleCN: 地板是松木做的。
senses.why: Once a tree has a name, its timber takes the same name, because the material is only the tree after it has been cut and sawn.
senses.whyCN: 一种树有了名字，它的木材也就用同一个名字，因为木料不过是砍下锯开之后的树。

senses.title: To long for someone or something
senses.definition: to want someone or something very much, in a way that makes you unhappy
senses.definitionCN: 非常想要某人或某物，想到心里难受
senses.example: She pined for the sea she had left behind.
senses.exampleCN: 她苦苦思念着离开的那片海。
senses.why: The verb came from a different word, an Old English verb for torment; a longing that hurts was pictured as a slow torture, and that ache stayed inside the meaning.
senses.whyCN: 动词另有来源，是古英语中表示「折磨」的动词；令人难受的渴望被想象成一种缓慢的拷问，这份痛感就留在了词义里。

senses.title: To waste away with grief or longing
senses.definition: to become weak, thin and dull because of sorrow, illness or a long wait
senses.definitionCN: 因悲伤、疾病或长久等待而变得虚弱、消瘦、没有神采
senses.example: He pined away after the farm was sold.
senses.exampleCN: 农场卖掉之后，他日渐憔悴。
senses.why: If longing is a torture, the body eventually shows it; pine away names the visible result of that inner strain rather than the feeling itself.
senses.whyCN: 既然渴望是一种折磨，身体迟早会把它显出来；pine away 指的就是这份内在煎熬露在外表上的结果，而不是那股情绪本身。

intro.en: Two different words meet in this spelling: the tree name came from Latin pinus, while the verb for painful longing came from an Old English verb for tormenting.
intro.cn: 这个拼写里其实合流了两个不同的词：树名来自拉丁语 pinus，表示痛苦渴望的动词则来自古英语中表示折磨的动词。

items.en: Latin pinus named the pine tree and could also mean its wood or resin; the same name travelled around the Mediterranean.
items.cn: 拉丁语 pinus 是松树的名字，也可指松木或松脂；同一个名称在地中海各地通行。

items.en: Old English borrowed the tree name as pin, and the modern spelling later added a final e to match the verb.
items.cn: 古英语把树名借入写作 pin，现代拼写后来加了一个词尾 e，好与动词的写法统一。

items.en: A separate Old English verb pinian meant to torture or torment; it came from pin, a noun for pain that is generally traced back to Latin poena.
items.cn: 另有一个古英语动词 pinian，意为折磨、拷问；它来自表示痛苦的名词 pin，而这个词一般认为可追溯到拉丁语 poena。

items.en: Middle English kept both words, so pinen could mean to suffer and also to yearn painfully for something lost.
items.cn: 中古英语把两个词都保留下来，于是 pinen 既指受苦，也指为失去的东西痛苦地思念。

items.en: Modern English holds the tree, its timber, the ache of longing and the visible wasting away, with the two histories now written as one word.
items.cn: 现代英语同时容纳了树、木材、思念之苦与看得见的消瘦，两段来历如今写成同一个词。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the tree's own family and a few words that only look similar; the near-meaning group pairs other conifers with other verbs of longing.
note.cn: 形近组收这棵树自己的词族，以及几个只是看起来相似的词；近义组把其他针叶树与别的「渴望」动词配在一起。

entries.definition: A small thin piece of metal for fastening cloth; it comes from a Latin word for a point or peg, so it is close in spelling but not in origin.
entries.definitionCN: 固定布料用的小金属针；它来自拉丁语中表示尖点或木钉的词，所以只是拼写相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: Shaped like a pine cone, as in the small gland deep in the brain.
entries.definitionCN: 形状像松果的，如大脑深处那个小腺体。

entries.definition: The fruit was named after the pine cone, which early English speakers thought it resembled.
entries.definitionCN: 这种水果因外形被早期英语使用者比作松果而得名。

entries.definition: A place where pine trees are grown.
A tall evergreen tree with flat needles and upright cones.
entries.definitionCN: 一种高大的常绿树，叶扁平，球果直立；冷杉。

entries.definition: An evergreen tree with short needles and hanging cones.
entries.definitionCN: 一种常绿树，针叶短，球果下垂；云杉。

entries.definition: A tree with needle-like leaves that turn yellow and fall in autumn.
entries.definitionCN: 针叶在秋天变黄脱落的树；落叶松。

entries.definition: To feel a strong, sad desire for something.
entries.definitionCN: 对某物怀有强烈而带苦味的向往。

normalIntro.en: A tree name and a verb of torment happen to share one spelling, and the whole family divides neatly between wood and longing.
normalIntro.cn: 一个树名和一个表示折磨的动词恰好共用一个拼写，整个词族也就清楚地分成「木」与「渴望」两半。

normal.en: Latin pinus is the tree, which is why botany still uses pinus for the genus and why pine needles resist frost.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 pinus 就是这种树，所以植物学至今用 pinus 作属名，松针也才那么耐霜。

normal.en: The verb pine never grew out of the tree; it came from an Old English word for torment, so pine for and pine tree are only spelling twins.
normal.cn: 动词 pine 并不是从树长出来的，它来自古英语中表示折磨的词，所以 pine for 与 pine tree 只是拼写上的双胞胎。

normal.en: Pine away adds away to the verb: the person is not only longing but visibly losing weight and colour.
normal.cn: pine away 在动词后加 away：人不只是思念，还肉眼可见地掉肉、褪色。

normal.en: Pinery uses -ery, the same place suffix as in bakery and brewery, so it means a place of pines.
normal.cn: pinery 用 -ery，与 bakery、brewery 里那个表场所的后缀相同，所以意思是「松树之地」。

normal.en: Pineal keeps the cone image: the gland was named for its shape, not for any connection with timber.
normal.cn: pineal 保留了松果的形象：那个腺体是因形状得名，与木材没有关系。

abstract.en: A pine keeps its needles all winter, and English keeps two unrelated words under one spelling just as stubbornly.
abstract.cn: 松树整个冬天都不落叶，英语也同样固执地把两个不相干的词留在一个拼写下。

abstract.en: The same four letters can mean shade, floorboards, heartache and weight loss, which is a reminder that context does the sorting.
abstract.cn: 同样四个字母可以指树荫、地板、心痛与消瘦，这提醒人：分辨词义的是上下文。

abstract.en: To pine is to be pulled toward something absent; the tree simply stands where it is, which is why the two images never mix.
abstract.cn: pine 是被拉向缺席之物；而松树只是站在原地，所以这两个意象从不混淆。

examples.en: An old pine shades the whole yard.
examples.cn: 一棵老松为整个院子遮阴。

examples.en: She pined for the sea she had left behind.
examples.cn: 她苦苦思念着离开的那片海。

examples.en: The floor is made of pine.
examples.cn: 地板是松木做的。

latinIntro.en: The tree comes from one Latin word and the ache of longing from another; both links are well attested, unlike the folk guess that the verb grew out of the tree.

senses.title: The place where someone lives
senses.definition: the house or place in which a person lives
senses.definitionCN: 一个人居住的房子或地方
senses.example: The president's residence stands by the river.
senses.exampleCN: 总统官邸位于河岸边。
senses.why: The noun names the place produced by residing.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词指居住这一行为所产生的场所。

senses.title: The act or period of living somewhere
senses.definition: the fact of living in a place, often used in official language
senses.definitionCN: 在某地居住的事实，常用于官方语言
senses.example: She took up residence in Paris last year.
senses.exampleCN: 她去年开始在巴黎居住。
senses.why: Residence can name the state of living there, not only the building.

senses.title: A large impressive house

senses.definitionCN: 大型而正式的住宅，尤指官邸
senses.example: The family moved to a smaller residence.

senses.whyCN: 「住所」的正式说法常带有规模与体面的意味。

intro.en: Residence comes from Latin residentia, a staying behind, from residere, to remain, through Old French residence.
intro.cn: residence 来自拉丁语 residentia（停留），源于 residere（留下），经古法语 residence 进入英语。

items.en: Sedere means to sit.
items.cn: sedere 意为坐。

items.en: Residere means to remain behind or dwell.
items.cn: residere 意为留下、居住。

items.en: Residentia means a staying behind or a dwelling.
items.cn: residentia 意为停留、居所。

items.en: Residence means a place of dwelling.
items.cn: residence 意为居住之处。

items.en: English residence names both the act and the place of living.
items.cn: 到 14 世纪，英语 residence 兼指居住行为与住所。

items.en: Modern English uses residence for homes, permits, and official dwellings.
items.cn: 现代英语中，residence 用于住宅、居留许可与官邸。

note.en: Residence is the noun of residing, and it sits near its family and near words for home and dwelling.
note.cn: residence 是 reside 的名词，与自身词族以及表示家和住所的词相邻。

normalIntro.en: Residence is the noun of reside: the place or fact of staying.
normalIntro.cn: residence 是 reside 的名词：停留的场所或事实。

normal.en: Take up residence means begin living somewhere.

normal.en: An official residence is a home provided for a leader.

normal.en: Residence permit names the right to live in a country.

normal.en: A residence can be modest or grand.

normal.en: Compare home: home is emotional, while residence is formal.

abstract.en: Picture one lit window in a dark row of houses.
abstract.cn: 想象一排黑暗的房子里，只有一扇窗亮着。

abstract.en: Imagine an address written carefully on a form.
abstract.cn: 想象地址被工整地写在表格上。

abstract.en: Think of a door key kept for many years.
abstract.cn: 想象一把保存多年的门钥匙。

examples.en: The president's residence stands by the river.

examples.cn: 她去年开始在巴黎居住。

examples.en: The family moved to a smaller residence.

dict_mnemonic.text: 「reside + ence」——居住这件事或这个地方，就是住所；这只是构词联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 sedere（坐）→ residere（留下、居住）→ residentia（停留、居所）→ 古法语 residence → 现代英语 residence。

sensesIntro.en: The noun names a dwelling, then the state of living there, and finally a large formal home such as an official one.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个名词先指住所，再指居住状态，最后指大型正式住宅，如官邸。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a lit window that marks one person's fixed home.
core.cn: 核心意象：一扇亮着的窗，标记着一个人固定的家。

branches.en: The physical home is the main modern sense.
branches.cn: 物理住所，是现代主要义项。

branches.en: The act of living there appears in official phrases.
branches.cn: 居住行为出现在官方短语中。

branches.en: A grand house adds dignity to the same word.
branches.cn: 宏伟住宅为同一个词增添体面意味。

branches.en: The building and the fact of living there depend on each other.
branches.cn: 建筑与居住事实彼此依存。

branches.en: Official residence joins the legal and the grand senses.
branches.cn: official residence 把法律含义与宏伟含义结合起来。

intro.en: Residence is an English -ence noun built on the Latin verb residere.
intro.cn: residence 是建立在拉丁动词 residere 上的英语 -ence 名词。

latinIntro.en: Latin sedere means to sit, residere means to remain, and residentia means a dwelling.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 sedere 意为坐，residere 意为留下，residentia 意为居所。

senses.title: Very enjoyable

items.en: Glorious named what deserved honour.

items.en: It widened to mean splendid and then delightful.

normalIntro.en: Glorious is glory turned into an adjective.

abstract.en: Glorious is light that people agree to remember.

sensesIntro.en: Glorious means worthy of honour, splendid to see, or very enjoyable.

definition_zh: 奇迹；神迹；奇迹般的事；非凡成就；典范
definition_en: an extraordinary event believed to come from divine power; also any astonishing achievement, or a wonderful example of a craft
core_image: 干涸的石池底忽然涌出清水，围观的人一时说不出话
scene: 旱季的村口，人们围着那口多年见底的老井，清晨时井底竟重新有了水。 The villagers called the refilled well a miracle.
sceneCN: 这里是「奇迹、神迹」（第 1 个义项：超出常理、被认为是神力所致的事）；句意为村民把重新蓄水的老井称作奇迹。图中可辨识物件：老井、水桶、围观的人群。

derivatives.zh: 由 miracle 词干加 -ous 构成，义为「奇迹般的；不可思议的」
由 miraculous 加 -ly 构成，义为「奇迹般地」
由 miracle 与 worker 复合，义为「创造奇迹的人」

senses.title: An event believed to come from divine power
senses.definition: an extraordinary event that cannot be explained by natural laws and is believed to be caused by divine power
senses.definitionCN: 无法用自然规律解释、被认为是神力所致的非凡事件
senses.example: Pilgrims came to the shrine hoping to witness a miracle.
senses.exampleCN: 朝圣者来到圣殿，希望能亲眼见到一次神迹。
senses.why: Latin miraculum named the thing that makes a person wonder, and religious writing applied it to events that only divine power could account for.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 miraculum 指「让人惊奇的东西」，宗教写作把它用在只有神力才能解释的事件上。

senses.title: An astonishing escape or achievement
senses.definition: a remarkable outcome that seemed impossible, such as a narrow escape or an achievement against the odds
senses.definitionCN: 看似不可能却发生了的非凡结果，如死里逃生或逆境中的成就
senses.example: It was a miracle that no one was hurt in the crash.
senses.exampleCN: 撞车事故中没有人受伤，真是奇迹。
senses.why: Once the word named what natural law cannot explain, it easily extended to any result that defies expectation, above all a survival nobody thought possible.
senses.whyCN: 既然这个词指自然规律解释不了的事，它就很容易扩展到任何违背预期的结果，尤其是原本认为不可能的幸存。

senses.title: A wonderful example of a craft
senses.definition: a thing so excellent or finely made that it fills the observer with wonder, as in a miracle of engineering
senses.definitionCN: 精巧或优异到让观者惊叹的事物，如工程上的奇迹
senses.example: The old bridge is a miracle of stonework and patience.
senses.exampleCN: 这座古桥是石工与耐心的奇迹。
senses.why: A structure that makes engineers wonder deserves the same word as a holy wonder, because wonder is the shared response rather than the cause.
senses.whyCN: 让工程师惊叹的建筑配得上与神圣奇观相同的词，因为共同点是观者的惊叹，而不是成因。

intro.en: Miracle goes back to a Latin verb meaning to wonder, whose noun named the thing that caused the wonder, and it entered English through French religious writing.
intro.cn: miracle 可追到一个意为「惊奇」的拉丁动词，其名词指引起惊奇的那个东西，再经法语宗教文本进入英语。

items.en: Mirari meant to wonder at or to be amazed by something; the deeper origin of the verb is generally regarded as uncertain.
items.cn: mirari 意为对某物感到惊奇、惊叹；这个动词更早的来源一般认为不确定。

items.en: Miraculum named an object of wonder, a marvel, and early Christian Latin narrowed it to an event beyond nature.
items.cn: miraculum 指令人惊奇之物、奇观，早期基督教拉丁语把它收窄为超自然的事件。

items.en: Old French miracle meant a holy wonder and also named the religious plays staged around such stories.
items.cn: 古法语 miracle 指神圣的奇事，也用来称呼围绕这类故事上演的宗教剧。

items.en: Middle English miracle covered both the holy event and the tale told about it, and the drama sense slowly faded.
items.cn: 中古英语的 miracle 既指神圣事件，也指讲述它的事迹，戏剧的意思后来慢慢消失。

items.en: Modern English widened the word to astonishing escapes and to excellent works, so a bridge can now be called a miracle.
items.cn: 现代英语把这个词扩展到惊人的脱险与出色的作品，于是一座桥如今也能被称作奇迹。

note.en: The look-alike group collects words built on the Latin verb for wondering; the near-meaning group collects other names for astonishing things.
note.cn: 形近组收建立在拉丁语「惊奇」动词上的词；近义组收其他表示惊人事物的名称。

entries.definition: Brought about as if by a miracle; astonishing.
entries.definitionCN: 仿佛由奇迹促成的；令人惊叹的。

entries.definition: An optical illusion, such as water appearing in a desert.
entries.definitionCN: 光学幻景，如沙漠中看似出现的水。

entries.definition: To regard someone or something with wonder and approval.
entries.definitionCN: 带着惊叹与赞许地看待某人或某物。

entries.definition: A reflective glass, or something that shows a faithful image.
entries.definitionCN: 反光的镜子，或忠实映现事物的东西。

entries.definition: A feeling of surprise and awe at something remarkable.
entries.definitionCN: 面对非凡事物时的惊讶与敬畏。

entries.definition: A wonderful thing, or to be filled with wonder at it.
entries.definitionCN: 奇妙的事物；对其感到惊叹。

entries.definition: Something extraordinary, often a person with exceptional talent.
entries.definitionCN: 非凡之物，常指天赋异禀的人。

entries.definition: A fact or event that can be observed, especially an unusual one.
entries.definitionCN: 可观察到的事实或事件，尤指不寻常的。

normalIntro.en: One Latin verb for wondering stands behind the whole family, so miracle, mirage, mirror and admire all keep a trace of awe.
normalIntro.cn: 一个表示「惊奇」的拉丁动词支撑着整个词族，所以 miracle、mirage、mirror 与 admire 都留着惊叹的痕迹。

normal.en: Mirari is Latin for to wonder, and miraculum is the thing that makes the wondering happen.
normal.cn: mirari 在拉丁语中意为「惊奇」，miraculum 就是引起这份惊奇的那个东西。

normal.en: Miracle reached English through Old French, where it already meant a holy wonder rather than any surprise.
normal.cn: miracle 经古法语进入英语，在法语里它已经指神圣的奇事，而不是随便什么意外。

normal.en: Mirage, mirror and admire descend from the same verb, which is why a desert illusion and a looking glass feel related to wonder.
normal.cn: mirage、mirror 与 admire 出自同一个动词，所以沙漠幻景与镜子在语感上都与惊奇有关。

normal.en: Miracle play was the medieval name for drama on holy subjects, a sense that English later dropped.
normal.cn: miracle play 是中世纪对宗教题材戏剧的称呼，这层意思后来被英语舍弃。

normal.en: The plural miracles stays countable: the word names single events, not a general mood of awe.
normal.cn: 复数 miracles 保持可数：这个词指一个个单独的事件，而不是笼统的敬畏气氛。

abstract.en: Picture a dry stone basin filling overnight while a crowd stands speechless.
abstract.cn: 想象干涸的石池一夜之间蓄满水，人群围着说不出话。

abstract.en: A word born from wonder can end up naming a bridge, because awe does not ask what caused the thing it admires.
abstract.cn: 一个从惊奇里生出的词最后可以指一座桥，因为惊叹并不追问被赞叹之物的成因。

abstract.en: What counts as a miracle depends on what a community believes is possible, so the word always carries a shared limit.
abstract.cn: 什么算奇迹取决于一个群体认为什么才可能，所以这个词总带着一条共同的边界。

examples.en: The villagers called the refilled well a miracle.
examples.cn: 村民把重新蓄水的老井称作奇迹。

examples.en: It was a miracle that no one was hurt in the crash.
examples.cn: 撞车事故中没有人受伤，真是奇迹。

examples.en: The bridge is a miracle of engineering.
examples.cn: 这座桥是工程上的奇迹。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「米拉可」——米拉可一挥手，干井冒出水，众人称奇；记住 miracle 是奇迹。

root: 拉丁语 mirari（惊奇）派生 miraculum（令人惊奇之物），经古法语 miracle 进入英语；同族词包括 mirage、mirror 与 admire。

sensesIntro.en: The core is an event that makes people wonder; the senses divide into the sacred event, the astonishing escape, and the excellent work that provokes the same awe.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「让人惊叹的事件」；义项分到神圣事件、惊人的脱险，以及引起同样惊叹的出色作品。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a dry stone basin filling with water overnight while a crowd watches.
core.cn: 核心意象：干涸的石池一夜蓄满水，众人围观。

branches.en: pilgrims standing before a shrine
branches.cn: 朝圣者站在圣殿前

branches.en: a family walking away from a crushed car
branches.cn: 一家人从撞毁的车旁走开

branches.en: a stone bridge holding after a flood
branches.cn: 洪水过后仍然站着的石桥

branches.en: the same astonishment felt at a shrine and at a crash
branches.cn: 在圣殿与在车祸现场感到的同一种惊叹

branches.en: a result nobody expected and a work nobody thought possible
branches.cn: 没人料到的结果与没人认为可能的作品

intro.en: The Latin verb for wondering and its noun for a wonder form the stem, while English suffixes and sharing relatives carry the family outward.
intro.cn: 拉丁语中表示「惊奇」的动词及其名词提供词干，英语后缀与同源词则把词族向外带开。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

items.meaning: to wonder at, to be amazed
a wonder, an object of wonder
brought about as if by a miracle
full of, having the quality of
an optical illusion of water in the desert
to regard with wonder and approval

definition_zh: 肥料；化肥；促使发展的东西
definition_en: a substance added to soil to help plants grow, especially a chemical product, or something that helps an idea develop
core_image: 白色颗粒从袋口倒进土里，很快被雨水洇湿
scene: 他把一袋白色颗粒均匀撒进田里。 Farmers spread fertilizer on the fields.
sceneCN: 这里 fertilizer 是「肥料」（第 1 个义项）；句意：农民把肥料撒在田里。

derivatives.zh: 施肥；使受精
施肥；受精
肥沃的
肥沃；生育力

senses.title: Substance for soil
senses.definition: a substance added to soil to help plants grow
senses.definitionCN: 加入土壤以帮助植物生长的物质
senses.example: Farmers spread fertilizer on the fields.
senses.exampleCN: 农民把肥料撒在田里。
senses.why: This is the general agricultural sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是通用的农业义。

senses.title: Chemical product
senses.definition: a manufactured chemical product used on crops
senses.definitionCN: 用于农作物的工业化化学产品
senses.example: The factory makes nitrogen fertilizer.
senses.exampleCN: 这家工厂生产氮肥。
senses.why: Modern farming relies on chemical fertilizers.
senses.whyCN: 现代农业依赖化学肥料。

senses.title: Something that promotes growth
senses.definition: something that helps an idea or process develop
senses.definitionCN: 帮助某种想法或过程发展的东西
senses.example: Praise is fertilizer for young talent.
senses.exampleCN: 赞赏是年轻人才成长的养料。
senses.why: The farming image can describe ideas.
senses.whyCN: 农业意象可以被用来形容想法。

intro.en: Fertilizer is fertilize plus -er, built on fertile, from Latin fertilis.
intro.cn: fertilizer 由 fertilize 加 -er 构成，而 fertilize 出自 fertile（拉丁语 fertilis）。

items.en: Fertilis meant able to bear fruit.
items.cn: fertilis 意为能结果实的。

items.en: Fertile entered English in the Middle Ages.
items.cn: fertile 在中世纪进入英语。

items.en: Fertilize meant to make land fruitful.
items.cn: fertilize 意为使土地丰产。

items.en: Fertilizer named the substance used.
items.cn: fertilizer 用来指所施用的物质。

items.en: Chemical fertilizers changed farming.
items.cn: 化学肥料改变了农业。

note.en: Fertilizer is compared with similar-looking words and with words for soil additives.
note.cn: 把 fertilizer 与形近词以及表示土壤添加物的词作比较。

entries.definition: to add fertilizer or make able to grow
able to produce good crops
the quality of being fertile
animal waste used to enrich soil
decayed plant matter used as fertilizer
a substance that helps growth

normalIntro.en: Fertilizer is the substance that makes soil fertile.
normalIntro.cn: fertilizer 就是让土壤变肥沃的物质。

normal.en: Fertilizer is fertilize plus -er.
normal.cn: fertilizer 是 fertilize 加 -er。

normal.en: Too much fertilizer can harm a field.
normal.cn: 肥料过多反而会伤害田地。

normal.en: Organic fertilizer comes from plants or animals.
normal.cn: 有机肥来自植物或动物。

normal.en: Nitrogen is a key part of many fertilizers.
normal.cn: 氮是许多肥料的关键成分。

normal.en: The verb is fertilize, the adjective fertile.
normal.cn: 动词是 fertilize，形容词是 fertile。

abstract.en: Fertilizer speeds growth but cannot replace soil.
abstract.cn: 肥料能加速生长，却替代不了土壤。

abstract.en: Good conditions matter more than any single additive.
abstract.cn: 好的环境比任何单一添加物都重要。

abstract.en: What feeds a field can also poison a river.
abstract.cn: 滋养田地的东西，也可能污染河流。

examples.en: Farmers spread fertilizer on the fields.
examples.cn: 农民把肥料撒在田里。

examples.en: The factory makes nitrogen fertilizer.
examples.cn: 这家工厂生产氮肥。

examples.en: Praise is fertilizer for young talent.
examples.cn: 赞赏是年轻人才成长的养料。

dict_mnemonic.text: fertilizer 由 fertilize（施肥）加 -er 构成，指施入土壤、帮助植物生长的物质，即肥料。

root: 由 fertile（肥沃的）派生的 fertilize 加 -er 构成，核心义「使土地丰产之物」。

sensesIntro.en: Fertilizer means a soil additive, a chemical product, or something that promotes growth.
sensesIntro.cn: fertilizer 意为肥料、化肥或促进发展的因素。

core.en: A substance that feeds the ground.
core.cn: 给土地提供养分的物质。

branches.en: Something added to help plants.
branches.cn: 加进去帮助植物生长的东西。

branches.en: A factory-made product for crops.
branches.cn: 工厂制造、用于农作物的产品。

branches.en: An image for what helps ideas grow.
branches.cn: 比喻帮助想法成长的养料。

branches.en: The general and chemical senses overlap.
branches.cn: 通用义与化肥义相互重叠。

branches.en: Both feed something that is growing.
branches.cn: 两者都在滋养正在生长的东西。

intro.en: Fertilizer shares the fertile family of growth words.
intro.cn: fertilizer 与 fertile 同属表示「生长」的词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin fertilis and ferre are the historical base.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 fertilis 与 ferre 是历史词根。

items.example: They fertilize the garden each spring.
items.exampleCN: 他们每年春天给花园施肥。

items.meaning: the act of enriching or fertilizing an egg
items.example: Fertilization took place in the lab.
The soil is dark and fertile.
The slope is dry and infertile.

items.exampleCN: 这项研究考察土壤贫瘠问题。

items.example: Fertilizing too early can burn roots.

definition_zh: 牺牲；献出；祭品
definition_en: to give up something valuable; to offer something to a god; the thing given up or offered
core_image: 把珍贵的东西郑重地放上祭台
scene: 父母为孩子牺牲了很多个人时间。 The parents sacrificed a lot of personal time for their children.
sceneCN: 这里 sacrifice 是「牺牲、放弃」（第 1 个义项）；句意：父母为孩子牺牲了很多个人时间。

derivatives.zh: 献祭的；牺牲性的
以牺牲的方式
献祭者

senses.title: Give up something
senses.definition: to give up something valuable for a purpose
senses.definitionCN: 为了某个目的放弃有价值的东西
senses.example: She sacrificed her career for the family.
senses.exampleCN: 她为了家庭放弃了自己的事业。
senses.why: The core sense is giving up something valued.
senses.whyCN: 核心义是放弃珍视之物。

senses.title: Offer to a god
senses.definition: to offer something to a god in a ceremony
senses.definitionCN: 在仪式中把某物献给神
senses.example: They sacrificed a goat at the temple.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在神庙献祭了一只山羊。
senses.why: Giving up becomes a sacred offering.
senses.whyCN: 放弃变成神圣的奉献。

senses.title: The cost borne
senses.definition: the thing given up for a purpose
senses.definitionCN: 为某个目的而放弃的东西
senses.example: The plan required great sacrifice.
senses.exampleCN: 这个计划需要巨大牺牲。
senses.why: The act becomes the cost itself.
senses.whyCN: 动作变成所承受的代价。

intro.en: Sacrifice comes from Latin sacrificium, a sacred offering.
intro.cn: sacrifice 源自拉丁语 sacrificium，意为神圣的供奉。

items.en: Sacer means holy or sacred.
items.cn: sacer 意为神圣的。

items.en: Facere means to make or do.
items.cn: facere 意为制作、做。

items.en: Sacrificium joins holy and making.
items.cn: sacrificium 把「神圣」与「做」结合。

items.en: Sacrifice keeps the offering sense.
items.cn: sacrifice 保留供奉之义。

items.en: Sacrifice covers both rite and cost.
items.cn: sacrifice 兼指仪式与代价。

items.en: Personal sacrifice becomes common usage.
items.cn: personal sacrifice 成为常见说法。

note.en: Sacrifice is giving up; to suffice is to be enough.
note.cn: sacrifice 是放弃，suffice 则是足够。

entries.definition: to be enough
holy
disrespect for something holy
to stop having or doing
to present something
to give up control

normalIntro.en: Sacrifice is giving up something precious for something more important.
normalIntro.cn: sacrifice 是为更重要的东西放弃珍贵之物。

normal.en: Many parents sacrifice their own comfort.
normal.cn: 许多父母牺牲自己的舒适。

normal.en: The villagers sacrificed food at the harvest.
normal.cn: 村民在收获时献上食物。

normal.en: Victory came at a heavy sacrifice.
normal.cn: 胜利以沉重牺牲为代价。

normal.en: He sacrificed sleep to finish the work.
normal.cn: 他为完成工作牺牲了睡眠。

normal.en: The team made great sacrifices for the project.
normal.cn: 团队为这个项目作出了巨大牺牲。

abstract.en: Picture a prized object laid on a stone altar.
abstract.cn: 想象一件珍贵之物被放在石祭台上。

abstract.en: Imagine letting go of something you love.
abstract.cn: 想象放开你喜爱的东西。

abstract.en: Think of a candle burning itself to give light.
abstract.cn: 想象蜡烛燃烧自己照亮别人。

examples.en: She sacrificed her free time to help the club.
examples.cn: 她牺牲空闲时间来帮助俱乐部。

examples.en: The ancient rite involved a sacrifice.
examples.cn: 这种古老仪式包含献祭。

examples.en: Success here demands real sacrifice.
examples.cn: 在这里取得成功需要真正的牺牲。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「sacrifice」里有 sacri（神圣）：把珍贵的东西献给更重要的目标，就是「牺牲、献祭」。

root: 拉丁语 sacrificium 由 sacer（神圣的）与 facere（做）构成，核心义「做神圣之事、献上供物」。

sensesIntro.en: Sacrifice means to give something up, to offer it to a god, or the cost that is borne.
sensesIntro.cn: sacrifice 意为放弃某物、向神献祭，或所承受的代价。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: something precious placed on an altar.
core.cn: 核心意象：珍贵之物被放上祭台。

branches.en: The base sense is giving up something valued.
branches.cn: 基础义是放弃珍视之物。

branches.en: Giving up becomes a sacred offering.
branches.cn: 放弃变成神圣供奉。

branches.en: The act becomes the cost borne.
branches.cn: 动作变成承受的代价。

branches.en: What you give up is the cost.
branches.cn: 你所放弃的正是代价。

branches.en: Everyday loss and ritual offering share the act.
branches.cn: 日常损失与仪式供奉共享同一动作。

intro.en: Sacrifice joins Latin sacer (holy) and facere (to make).
intro.cn: sacrifice 由拉丁语 sacer（神圣）与 facere（做）组合。

latinIntro.en: Latin sacer, facere, and sacrificium are the source forms.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 sacer、facere 与 sacrificium 是来源词形。

items.example: Facere means to perform a rite.
